**Short answer:** The data doesn't show suicide prevention growing as an OIG theme. Reports with a suicide-related recommendation fell from 2024 to 2025. The counts can't tell you why.

**Counts** (data as of 2026-11-04, 13 days old, not stale). These are reports with at least one recommendation containing the keyword "suicide", grouped by publication year:

| Year | Reports | Recommendations | Still open |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | 56 | 98 | 0 |
| 2025 | 11 | 19 | 6 |

**What the counts can show**
- Recommendations that mention suicide were much less common in 2025 reports than in 2024 reports (11 vs. 56).
- Every 2024 recommendation is closed as implemented. Six of the 2025 ones remain open. Median time to closure was about 232 days for 2024 and 242 days for 2025.

**What they cannot show**
- **Why the count fell.** A drop could mean problems improved. It could also mean OIG changed its inspection protocols, its report volume, or its focus. For example, a 2024 cluster of similar inspection reports could account for much of the 56. I haven't checked that.
- **Whether it is a "theme."** This is a keyword match on recommendation text. It misses recommendations that cover suicide prevention without using the word "suicide." It also catches recommendations where suicide is only mentioned in passing. It is not OIG's own topic tag, and OIG tagged only about a quarter of reports with topics.
- **Severity or quality.** Counts of reports and recommendations don't measure how serious the findings were or how well facilities performed. They also don't compare facilities.
- **A trend.** Two years is too short to establish a trend. The 2025 figure may also be lower because recommendations from recent reports haven't all been published yet or fully entered. I can't confirm that from this data.
- **Closure timing.** 2025 reports have had less time to close, so the open and closed figures aren't comparable between the two years. The data can't establish whether target dates were met.

I can break this down by report type, check the "Suicide Prevention" topic tag, or look at 2023 and earlier years for context. Tell me which you want.

**The median for VBA recommendations is 179 days.** The data is as of 2026-11-04 and is not stale.

**What the number measures:** It is the time from a report's publication to the date OIG recorded the recommendation as closed. It covers closed recommendations only. The sample is 914 of the 923 closed VBA recommendations. About 6% of closed recommendations nationwide have no closure date on OIG's site and are left out.

- **Typical range:** The middle half of closures took 134 to 312.5 days (the first and third quartiles).
- **Same-day closures:** 110 of the 914 closed on the day the report was published. These were presumably resolved beforehand, and they pull the median down.
- **Volume:** VBA has 966 recommendations in total. 897 are closed as implemented, 26 are closed as not implemented, and 43 are still open.
- **Open items:** The median age of open items is 161 days. 17 have been open more than a year, and the oldest has been open 1,567 days. These open items are not in the 179-day median.

**Caveats:**
- The closure date appears to record when OIG closed the item after reviewing evidence. That can come months after VBA did the work, so 179 days is not a measure of how fast VBA acted.
- The figure does not show whether anyone met a target date. A target is the facility's own estimate, and a closure after it does not show a missed commitment.

I can't give you a percentage of VHA recommendations that missed their target dates. The data can't support that figure, so any number I gave would be a guess.

The reason is in how the dates are recorded. A target date is the facility's own estimate. The closure date appears to be when OIG closed the recommendation after reviewing evidence, and that can come months after the work was done. A closure after the target, or an open item past its target, therefore doesn't show that a facility missed its commitment.

Here is what the data does show for VHA as the action office (data as of 2026-11-04, 13 days old, not stale):

- **Total:** VHA has 13,440 recommendations.
- **Status:** 426 are open, 12,978 are closed as implemented, and 36 are closed as not implemented. The not-implemented rate is 0.28%.
- **Time to close:** The median is 225 days, and the middle half of recommendations closed between 153 and 326 days. This is based on 12,164 recommendations that have closure dates.
- **Closed on publication day:** 946 were closed the day the report came out.
- **Open items:**
  - The median age of an open item is 147 days.

- About 6% of closed recommendations, mostly from 2013 to 2016, have no closure date on OIG's site.
- 11 VHA recommendations were excluded from the time-to-close figures because their closure dates came out negative.
- A recommendation that names two offices counts for both, so group sizes can add up to more than the total.
- OIG's dashboard shows 586 open recommendations across all offices, while this data has 567. The difference is 19 blank rows on OIG's pages. A row-by-row comparison found the same recommendations in both.

I can't tell you what OIG will cite at El Paso's next inspection. OIG publishes no inspection schedule, and what an inspection finds can't be predicted from the public record. The data is current as of 2026-11-04 (13 days old). Here is what the record does show.

**Next inspection window (my estimate, not OIG's):** about January 2028. That is the latest inspection's end date (2025-01-16) plus roughly three years, based on the program's stated approximately three-year cycle. Publication usually comes months after an inspection, so an estimate based on it would run later.

**Most recent inspection:** [Report 25-00193-155](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/healthcare-facility-inspection/healthcare-facility-inspection-va-el-paso-healthcare-system), published 2026-07-16. It has two open recommendations:
1. Executive leaders ensure staff maintain a clean and safe environment (Environment of Care). The facility's target date is 2027-01-29.
2. The Medical Center Director ensures providers complete secondary toxic exposure screenings within 30 days (Primary Care). The facility's target date is 2026-12-31.

**Other open items:** [Report 23-01179-204](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/information-security-inspection/inspection-information-security-va-el-paso-healthcare), an information security inspection published 2023-09-27, has two open items. Both are addressed to OIT:
- Ensure a video surveillance system is operational and monitored for the data center.
- Ensure water detection sensors are implemented in the data center.

Open items are what remains unresolved. They are not a forecast of future citations. The facility has 19 reports and 66 recommendations in total, and the record shows no repeat findings for it.

**Themes cited at peer facilities (listed by how common they are, not by severity):**
- Workflows for communicating test results under VHA Directive 1088(1). This appears in 21 of 112 reports. One example is [Report 26-00057-170](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/healthcare-facility-inspection/healthcare-facility-inspection-va-shreveport-healthcare) (Shreveport).
- Facility policy and monitoring for notifying patients of test results. This appears in 12 of 112 reports. One example is [Report 24-00603-86](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/healthcare-facility-inspection/healthcare-facility-inspection-va-hampton-healthcare-system) (Hampton).
- Keeping a clean environment under VHA Directive 1608(1). This appears in 11 of 112 reports. One example is [Report 26-00030-213](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/healthcare-facility-inspection/healthcare-facility-inspection-salisbury-va-health-care) (Salisbury).
- Stable and consistent leadership. This appears in 9 of 112 reports.
- Clean and safe patient care areas. This appears in 9 of 112 reports.

None of El Paso's own recommendations fall in these groups. That doesn't mean the facility was never cited for similar themes, because related findings can sit in other groups. Peer actions are the closest matches by wording and may not all belong to the group. Facility target dates are each facility's own estimate.

Preparing against these themes and the open items is reasonable, but it won't tell you what the inspectors will actually cite.
